name: Eyjafjallajökull
description: Eyjafjallajökull is one of Iceland's most famous volcanoes. Its 2010 eruption caused widespread disruption to European aviation and demonstrated the powerful interaction between ice, water and magma.
geology: Located along Iceland's volcanic rift zone, Eyjafjallajökull is shaped by the interaction between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak, renowned for its towering near-symmetrical cone shape as well as inspiring centuries worth of Japanese art, literature and poetry.
geology: The stratovolcano is located on the Pacific ring of fire, at a triple junction between the Pacific, Phillipine and Eurasian plate.

name: Kilauea
description: Unlike other volcanoes, Kilauea erupts slowly and gently producing flowing 'pahoehoe' lava as opposed to highly explosive blasts.
geology: The shield volcano is fed by the Hawaiian hotspot - a lone mantle plume in the centre of the pacific plate.

name: Mount St. Helens
description: Mount St Helens is best known for its unexpected catastrophic 1980 eruption. An earthquake kickstarted a landslide, which triggered a sideways blast, devastating hundreds of square miles at hurricane speeds.
geology: The Volcano sits above the Cascadia Subduction Zone, where the partial melting of the Juan de Fuca plate results in magma-fuelled eruptions.

name: Etna
description: Mount Etna is Europe's most active volcano. Its frequent, spectacular eruptions constantly reshape Sicily's landscape and demonstrate the relentless power of persistent basaltic volcanism.
geology: Etna is a complex stratovolcano formed by the collision of the African and Eurasian plates, fueling its highly active and fluid magma system.

name: Krakatoa
description: The original Krakatoa volcano was destroyed in it's famous 1883 eruption, which is often described as 'the loudest sound in recorded history', heard up to 5,000 km away.
geology: Krakatoa lives on through Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa'), which demonstrates frequent, small eruptions.

name: Ojos del Salado
description: Sitting on the Chile - Argentina border, Ojos del Salado is the highest active volcano in the world.
geology: Ojos del Salado is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Nazca plate beneath the South American plate.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest peak in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.
geology: Mount Kilimanjaro is a complex stratovolcano formed by the East African Rift system, the same system responsible for most african volcanism today..

name: Mount Vesuvius
description: Mount Vesuvius is best known for its catastrophic eruption in 79 AD, which buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under a thick blanket of volcanic ash.
geology: Vesuvius is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the African plate beneath the Eurasian plate in the Mediterranean region.

name: Mount Elbrus
description: Mount Elbrus is the highest peak in Europe and one of the Seven Summits, attracting climbers from around the world.
geology: Elbrus is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Arabian plate beneath the Eurasian plate.

name: Mount Pelee
description: Mount Pelee is a stratovolcano located on the Caribbean island of Martinique. It is infamous for its catastrophic eruption in 1902, which destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre and killed nearly 30,000 people.
geology: Pelee is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the North American plate beneath the Caribbean plate.

name: Mount Merapi
description: Mount Merapi is one of Indonesia's most active volcanoes, known for its frequent eruptions and pyroclastic flows that pose significant hazards to nearby communities.
geology: Merapi is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Indo-Australian plate beneath the Eurasian plate.

name: Mount Warning
description: Mount Warning is a shield volcano located in New South Wales, Australia. It is the remnant of an ancient volcanic caldera and is known for its unique geological features and biodiversity.
geology: Mount Warning is a shield volcano formed by the eruption of basaltic lava flows during the Miocene epoch.

name: Mount Erebus
description: Mount Erebus is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, located on Ross Island in Antarctica. It is known for its persistent lava lake and unique ice fumaroles.
geology: Erebus is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Antarctic plate.

name: Mount Rainier
description: Mount Rainier is a massive stratovolcano located in Washington State, USA. It is the highest peak in the Cascade Range and is considered one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the United States due to its potential for lahars and pyroclastic flows.
geology: Rainier is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Juan de Fuca plate beneath the North American plate.

name: Mount Shasta
description: Mount Shasta is a prominent stratovolcano located in northern California, USA. It is part of the Cascade Range and is known for its stunning beauty and recreational opportunities.
geology: Shasta is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Juan de Fuca plate beneath the North American plate.

name: Mount Teide
description: Mount Teide is the highest peak in Spain and the third highest volcano in the world when measured from its base on the ocean floor. It is located on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands.
geology: Teide is a complex stratovolcano formed by the interaction of the African and Eurasian tectonic plates.

name: Mount Ruapehu
description: Mount Ruapehu is the largest active volcano in New Zealand and is located in the central North Island. It is known for its ski fields and the Tongariro National Park, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
geology: Ruapehu is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Australian plate.
